363374.title: Simple-digraph counterexample conjecture for fully directed bunkbed (Hollom Conj 6.2)
363374.why: Hollom's Conjecture 6.2 (arXiv:2406.01790v1, published Eur. J. Combin. 128 (2025) 104188) asks for a simple digraph D with BBC(E_8,D) false; E_8 = simple digraph + bidirected verticals + uniform random subgraph. Przybylwoski (arXiv:2506.22284v2, accepted EJC), Theorem 1.2 with Definition 4.1 constructs a simple acyclic digraph G_2^k with P(1^-->9^-) < P(1^-->9^+) under exactly this unconditioned uniform model: the conditioned counterexample G_1 is boosted by k+2-vertex gadgets replacing vertices 2,5,8, P(C_i)=1-(1-2^-5)^k -> 1. Direct public counterexample; body read and retained.
363374.evidence_level: primary_body_read (2506.01790v1 full body; 2506.22284v2 full body retained)
363374.notes: Not a campaign result. Scope check: Przybylowski's model is uniform over P(E(D-tilde)) = E_8 with p=1/2; graph is simple and acyclic, so it also answers Hollom's Question 6.3 negatively. Published-version correspondence not retrieved (EJC paywalled route not attempted).

377313.title: k-Schur involution conjecture (Lapointe-Morse 2001)
377313.why: The identity omega s_lambda^(k) = s_(lambda^omega_k)^(k) for every k-bounded partition lambda is a theorem of Lapointe-Morse, 'A k-tableau characterization of k-Schur functions' (arXiv:math/0505519; published Adv. in Appl. Math. 2006): from the e- and h-k-Pieri rules, applying omega to s_lambda^(k) produces exactly one k-Schur function, indexed by the k-conjugate. Independently quoted as shown in the published AMS memoir 'Quantum cohomology and the k-Schur basis' (Trans. AMS, eq. 3.6). The record's own source (math/0111192) proved it only for hook length <= k.
377313.notes: Not a campaign result. Retirement is from public sources; the exact theorem number/label in math/0505519 should be quoted from the body before any formal citation.

364119.title: Cayley-avoidance maximum inequality (Conj 8.8 of arXiv:2407.19583)
364119.why: Conjecture 8.8 (arXiv:2407.19583v1, published Australas. J. Combin. 94(2) (2025) 267-299), under the section preamble 'Let p and q be two Cayley permutations of the same length': if max(p) <= max(q) then |Cay_n(p)| >= |Cay_n(q)|. Counterexample: p=1122, q=1112 (both length 4, max=2); |Cay_5(p)|=520 < 522=|Cay_5(q)|. Also n=6: 4340 < 4394. Verified by two independent exact enumerations of the complete 541-word set Cay_5 (and 4683-word Cay_6); machinery validated against the source's own results (|Cay_n(112)|=|Cay_n(122)|=(n+1)!/2; source's check |Cay_n(13442)|=|Cay_n(14233)| for n<=7 reproduced). Published AJC version states the conjecture verbatim with no resolution; no public refutation found (searched 2026-10-30).
364119.mechanism: Complete finite counterexample: containment is subsequence rank-type matching (source Def.); the certificate is checkable by enumerating the 541 Cayley permutations of size 5 and counting avoiders.
364119.decisive_next_calculation: Done (scripts/decisive_cayley.py, scripts/verify_cayley_indep.py under the pinned helper guard). No remaining calculation needed for the refutation itself.
364119.certificate: Two length-4 patterns p=1122, q=1112 and n=5, with exact counts 520 and 522 over the full Cay_5; replay cost: enumeration of 541 words. Formalization: finite lists, decidable subsequence rank-type check; no axioms beyond standard.
364119.notes: PROPOSAL 1 (see proposals.json). Not merely a diagnostic: the exhibited witness makes the existentially quantified negation literally complete. Prior-art: no resolution in Cerbai-Claesson 2507.09304, Hertzsprung-patterns follow-up (2026), or elsewhere found; AJC published version retains the open conjecture.
